### Assessments of second speakership

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/5D4A2409_%2848996340263%29.jpg/250px-5D4A2409_%2848996340263%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:5D4A2409_(48996340263).jpg)Pelosi (center) with [Lloyd Nelson Hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Nelson_Hand "Lloyd Nelson Hand") and [Ann Hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Hand "Ann Hand") in 2019

As with her first tenure, experts gave Pelosi's second tenure as speaker high marks, with many opining that during her two tenures as speaker she had been among the most effective individuals to hold the position.

In June 2019, [Brent Budowsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brent_Budowsky "Brent Budowsky") opined in *[The Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hill_(newspaper) "The Hill (newspaper)")* that Pelosi had been "the most important, consequential and effective Speaker since Tip O'Neill" as well as "one of the greatest Speakers who ever served."[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-154) In January 2020, on the eve of Trump's [first impeachment trial before the U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_impeachment_trial_of_Donald_Trump "First impeachment trial of Donald Trump"), *Washington Post* political writer Paul Kane called Pelosi the most powerful House speaker in at least 25 years, noting that some historians were comparing her influence to that of former speaker Sam Rayburn.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-155) In 2021, former Republican speaker John Boehner opined that Pelosi had been the most powerful House speaker in U.S. history.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-156)

In November 2022, [Chris Cillizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Cillizza "Chris Cillizza") wrote that Pelosi was "the most effective speaker ever."[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-Cillizzamosteffective-152) Johnathan Bernstein opined for *The Washington Post* and *[Bloomberg News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News")* that Pelosi was "the greatest speaker in history."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-157) Jackie Calmes of the *[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")* shared the same opinion.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-158) Sarah Ferris of *Politico* called Pelosi "a legislative giant regarded as one of the most powerful speakers in modern U.S. history."[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-159) Historian Lindsay M. Chervinsky wrote for [NBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News "NBC News") that Pelosi was "one of the most effective speakers in history" and had been so while facing "the double standards that apply to powerful women."[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-Chervinsky-153)

John Haduk wrote for the Brookings Institution:
> Whether you agree with her politics or not, it is undeniable that [Pelosi] has been a remarkably effective House leader. That success has come as both House Minority Leader and as Speaker of the House. As Speaker, she has worked with a majority as large as 81 seats in November and December 2009 (258–177) and one as small as 6 seats from April to May 2021 (218–212).[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-160)

A number of progressive and liberal-leaning outlets published strong assessments of Pelosi's tenure. Harold Meyerson opined that Pelosi had been the greatest speaker in U.S. history in an article in *[The American Prospect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_American_Prospect "The American Prospect")*.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-161) Amanda Marcotte of *[Salon.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salon.com "Salon.com")* opined that Pelosi was the greatest speaker of all time, calling her "both the most effective and most progressive House speaker of all time." Marcotte added that Pelosi had been effective "both in terms of managing an unruly caucus and being able to push her party in more progressive directions."[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-162)

## Post–Democratic leadership (2023–present)

On November 29, 2022, the [Steering and Policy Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steering_and_Policy_Committees_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives "Steering and Policy Committees of the United States House of Representatives") of the House Democratic Caucus honorarily named Pelosi "speaker emerita" in the upcoming [118th U.S. Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/118th_U.S._Congress "118th U.S. Congress").[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-163)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-164) Her second speakership, and her participation in the House Democratic Party leadership, concluded on January 3, 2023, at the end of the [117th Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/117th_United_States_Congress "117th United States Congress").[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-165)

Amid concerns about President Biden's reelection prospects in the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"), Pelosi and other Democratic officials[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-166)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-167)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-168) urged him [to withdraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withdrawal_of_Joe_Biden_from_the_2024_United_States_presidential_election "Withdrawal of Joe Biden from the 2024 United States presidential election") his [candidacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2024_presidential_campaign "Joe Biden 2024 presidential campaign") before [the party's National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Democratic_National_Convention "2024 Democratic National Convention").[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-169) She feared that his faltering candidacy might not only result in Trump's victory but also have a [coattail effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coattail_effect "Coattail effect") that could bring Democrats defeat in the coinciding House and Senate elections, producing a Republican [government trifecta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_trifecta "Government trifecta"). On July 10, Pelosi said the party encouraged Biden to make the decision because time was running out.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-170) He withdrew from the race on July 21 and endorsed Vice President [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") as the party's presidential nominee.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-171) Before Biden withdrew, Pelosi had told other California congressional Democrats that she believed a competitive "open process" should determine the new Democratic candidate.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-172) She endorsed Harris within one day.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-173) Although Harris did not win any primary elections, Pelosi insisted that the process that led to Harris's nomination was a "primary": "We had an open primary, and she won it. Nobody else got in the race."[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-174) After Harris lost to Trump, Pelosi blamed Biden's late exit from the race and the lack of an open Democratic primary.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-175)

Pelosi is a member of the [House Baltic Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Baltic_Caucus "House Baltic Caucus") and the [Congressional Equality Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Equality_Caucus "Congressional Equality Caucus").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-176)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-177)

On November 6, 2025, Pelosi announced she would not seek reelection and would retire from the House of Representatives in 2027.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-178)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-179)

On October 21, 2026, Pelosi spoke at the [Internet Archive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_Archive "Internet Archive") in support of the organization and libraries.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-180)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-181)

## Post–political career

In 2026, Pelosi announced that she would co-teach a course on Congress with [Eric Schickler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Schickler "Eric Schickler"), a political science professor, at the [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley").[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-182)

## Political positions

Main article: [Political positions of Nancy Pelosi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_positions_of_Nancy_Pelosi "Political positions of Nancy Pelosi")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Ellison-20070104.jpg/250px-Ellison-20070104.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ellison-20070104.jpg)Pelosi and Representative [Keith Ellison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Ellison "Keith Ellison") at his swearing-in ceremony with [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson")'s [Quran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quran "Quran") in 2007

Pelosi was a founding member of the [Congressional Progressive Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Progressive_Caucus "Congressional Progressive Caucus"), which she left in 2003 after being elected House minority leader.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-183) She is still widely considered a liberal.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-184)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-185)

## Public image

Pelosi has often been described as a polarizing figure, facing criticism from both the political right and left. [Progressives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressivism_in_the_United_States "Progressivism in the United States") have criticized her for her knowledge of [waterboarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterboarding "Waterboarding") and other torture methods during the [war on terror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror "War on terror"), accusing her of not objecting strongly enough to these practices.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-:3-68) [Conservatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States") and [libertarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarianism_in_the_United_States "Libertarianism in the United States") have taken issue with her positions on [gun rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_keep_and_bear_arms "Right to keep and bear arms"), viewing her advocacy for [gun control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control "Gun control") as an infringement on [Second Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Second Amendment to the United States Constitution") rights.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-186) They have also criticized her stance on [taxation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxation_in_the_United_States "Taxation in the United States"), particularly her support for higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations to fund social programs.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-:3-68) Her role in leading the House to impeach President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") twice has drawn significant criticism from Trump supporters and Republicans, who perceived the impeachments as politically motivated and divisive.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-:3-68)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-187)

Pelosi has faced allegations of using her position for [insider trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insider_trading "Insider trading"), particularly concerning stock transactions that critics claim were influenced by her legislative knowledge.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-188) The return on the Pelosis' investment portfolio was 16,930% between 1987 and 2024, which beat the S&P 500 by 581%.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-:1-189) Critics have also depicted her as a symbol of the [liberal elite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_elite "Liberal elite"), pointing to her strong opposition to [populism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Populism_in_the_United_States "Populism in the United States") and comments suggesting that some Americans reject Democratic policies due to their beliefs about "guns, gays, [and] God".[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-:3-68)[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-190) During the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Pelosi was accused of hypocrisy when she had her hair styled at a salon that was supposed to be closed for indoor appointments due to health restrictions, with critics alleging she used her position to receive preferential treatment.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-191)

## Electoral history

Main article: [Electoral history of Nancy Pelosi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_history_of_Nancy_Pelosi "Electoral history of Nancy Pelosi")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Nancy_pelosi_drive.JPG/250px-Nancy_pelosi_drive.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nancy_pelosi_drive.JPG)The city of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") named a street in [Golden Gate Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gate_Park "Golden Gate Park") in honor of Pelosi after her many years representing the city in [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress").

Pelosi's only close race so far has been in the special election to succeed U.S. representative [Sala Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sala_Burton "Sala Burton") after her death in February 1987. Pelosi defeated San Francisco supervisor [Harry Britt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Britt "Harry Britt") in the Democratic primary with 36 percent of the vote to his 32 percent,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-nationnewface-18)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-192) then Republican Harriet Ross by more than 2-to-1.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-193) Since then, Pelosi has enjoyed overwhelming support in her political career, collecting 76 and 77 percent of the vote in [California's 5th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California's_5th_congressional_district "California's 5th congressional district") 1988 and 1990. In 1992, after the redistricting from the [1990 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_United_States_census "1990 United States census"), Pelosi ran in [California's 8th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California's_8th_congressional_district "California's 8th congressional district"), which now covered the San Francisco area. She has continued to post landslide victories since, dropping beneath 80 percent of the vote only four times in general elections since [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_California#District_8 "1992 United States House of Representatives elections in California"). After redistricting from the [2010 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"), Pelosi ran in [California's 12th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California's_12th_congressional_district "California's 12th congressional district"), which she represented for the next decade. Due to the [2020 United States redistricting cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_redistricting_cycle "2020 United States redistricting cycle") from the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Pelosi now represents [California's 11th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California's_11th_congressional_district "California's 11th congressional district"), which covers San Francisco.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-194)

## Personal life

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Speaker-Nancy-Pelosi-LBJ-Library.jpg/250px-Speaker-Nancy-Pelosi-LBJ-Library.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Speaker-Nancy-Pelosi-LBJ-Library.jpg)Pelosi at the [LBJ Presidential Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Baines_Johnson_Library_and_Museum "Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum") in 2022

Nancy D'Alesandro met [Paul Francis Pelosi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Pelosi "Paul Pelosi") while she was attending college.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-235) They married in Baltimore at the [Cathedral of Mary Our Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_of_Mary_Our_Queen,_Baltimore "Cathedral of Mary Our Queen, Baltimore") on September 7, 1963.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-236) They then moved to New York, followed by a move to San Francisco in 1969, where her husband's brother [Ronald Pelosi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Pelosi "Ron Pelosi") was a member of the [City and County of San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_and_County_of_San_Francisco "City and County of San Francisco")'s [Board of Supervisors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Supervisors "Board of Supervisors").[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-237)

Nancy and Paul Pelosi have five children, including [Christine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Pelosi "Christine Pelosi") and [Alexandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_Pelosi "Alexandra Pelosi"), and nine grandchildren.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-238) Alexandra, a journalist, covered the Republican presidential campaigns in 2000 and made a film about the experience, *[Journeys with George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journeys_with_George "Journeys with George")*. In 2007, Christine published a book, *Campaign Boot Camp: Basic Training for Future Leaders*.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-239)

Pelosi resides in the [Pacific Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Heights,_San_Francisco,_California "Pacific Heights, San Francisco, California") neighborhood of San Francisco.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-240)[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-241) Her 2016 financial disclosure report lists among her assets a combined home and vineyard in [St. Helena, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Helena,_California "St. Helena, California"), two commercial buildings in San Francisco, and a townhouse in [Loomis, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loomis,_California "Loomis, California").[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-242) In January 2021, her San Francisco home was vandalized with graffiti, messages of "[c]ancel rent" were left on her garage, along with fake blood and a severed pig's head.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-243)[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-244)

### Financial status

Pelosi's husband, Paul, is a wealthy investor and the primary source of the couple's wealth.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-245) In 2009, [OpenSecrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenSecrets "OpenSecrets") estimated Pelosi's net worth at $58 million, making her the 13th-wealthiest member of Congress.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-246)[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-247) *Business Insider* reported that Pelosi's net worth was $26.4 million in 2012 and made her the 13th-richest member of Congress.[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-Hickey-248) In 2014, OpenSecrets reported Pelosi's net worth had almost doubled, to about $101 million, making her the eighth-richest. In 2018, *Roll Call* estimated Pelosi's net worth at $16.0 million, making her the 30th-richest member.[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-Roll_Call_Wealth_of_Congress_Index_2014-249) As of 2021, Pelosi's net worth was valued at $120 million, making her the sixth-richest person in Congress.

#### Stock trading

*Roll Call* said Pelosi's earnings are connected to her husband's heavy investments in stocks that include [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_(Company) "Apple (Company)"), [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney"), [Comcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comcast "Comcast") and [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"). *Roll Call* reported that the couple have $13.46 million in liabilities including mortgages on seven properties. According to *Roll Call*, Pelosi and her husband hold properties "worth at least $23 million, including a St. Helena vineyard in [Napa Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_Valley "Napa Valley") worth at least $5 million."[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-Roll_Call_Wealth_of_Congress_Index_2014-249)

According to journalist [Glenn Greenwald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Greenwald "Glenn Greenwald"), the Pelosis have traded $33 million worth of tech stocks over the past two years, including Apple, [Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), Facebook, and [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google") stocks.[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-250) In May and June 2021, Pelosi's husband purchased stocks in tech companies such as [Alphabet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphabet_Inc. "Alphabet Inc."), Amazon, and Apple, netting a gain of $5.3 million. This occurred even while Speaker Pelosi was working on anti-trust legislation to better regulate the tech industry.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-251) The CEO of Apple, [Tim Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Cook "Tim Cook"), had called Pelosi to lobby her in opposition to the new regulations.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-252) Pelosi opposes increasing regulations on stock trades by members of congress, stating that "we're a free market economy" and congresspeople "should be able to participate in that."[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-253) This comment drew strong criticism, including from Democrats who favor banning stock trades by members of Congress.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-254)

Pelosi has faced scrutiny over her family's stock trading activities, particularly after reports indicated that her investment portfolio achieved a 54% return in 2024, outperforming many hedge funds and the S&P 500.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-255) Critics argue that members of Congress, including Pelosi, may have access to non-public information that could benefit personal investments, despite the STOCK Act of 2012, which prohibits insider trading by lawmakers.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-256)

In July 2024, Pelosi's husband, Paul Pelosi, sold between $500,000 and $1 million worth of Visa stock shortly before the Department of Justice filed an antitrust lawsuit against the company.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-257) This transaction drew allegations of potential insider trading. Pelosi's spokesperson said she does not own individual stocks and was not involved in her husband's investment decisions.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-258) No formal investigation or charges have been announced as of 2025.

The incident intensified bipartisan calls for new legislation banning stock trading by members of Congress and their immediate families. In response, Senator [Josh Hawley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Hawley "Josh Hawley") reintroduced the Preventing Elected Leaders from Owning Securities and Investments (PELOSI) Act in early 2025.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-259)

### Involvement in Italian-American community

Pelosi is a board member of the [National Organization of Italian American Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Organization_of_Italian_American_Women "National Organization of Italian American Women").[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-260) She served for 13 years as a board member of the National Italian American Foundation (NIAF). In 2007, she received the NIAF Special Achievement Award for Public Advocacy and remains involved in the foundation.[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-261)[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-262)

### Catholic church

Pelosi considers herself a "devout Catholic", but has had numerous disagreements with members of the church hierarchy over gay rights, abortion, contraception, and in vitro fertilization. She has said that her biggest disappointment was the church's lobbying against the Affordable Care Act because of contraception coverage.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-Calmes_LATimes-23)

Pelosi and Catholic bishops have also disagreed about [abortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion "Abortion") rights. Although she thought it was "lovely" that she had five children in a little over six years, she argued, "It's a woman's right to make her own choices with her family, her God, her doctor."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-Calmes_LATimes-23)

On May 20, 2022, [Salvatore Cordileone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvatore_Cordileone "Salvatore Cordileone"), [archbishop of San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_San_Francisco "Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Francisco"), announced that Pelosi would be barred from receiving [Holy Communion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Communion "Holy Communion") because of her support of [pro-choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion-rights_movements "Abortion-rights movements") abortion policies.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-263) Cordileone had communicated his concerns on April 7, 2022, writing, "should you not publicly repudiate your advocacy for abortion 'rights' or else refrain from referring to your Catholic faith in public and receiving Holy Communion, I would have no choice but to make a declaration, in keeping with [Canon 915](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canon_915 "Canon 915"), that you are not to be admitted to Holy Communion."[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-264)

On June 29, 2022, Pelosi received Communion at a Papal Mass presided over by [Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis") in Rome at [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter's_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica").[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-265)[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-266)

### Home invasion

Main article: [Attack on Paul Pelosi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Paul_Pelosi "Attack on Paul Pelosi")

In October 2022, while Pelosi was in Washington, D.C., an intruder entered her San Francisco home demanding to know her whereabouts, and attacked her husband, Paul Pelosi, with a hammer.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-NYT1031-267) The assailant, David DePape, was convicted on federal and state charges and sentenced to life without parole.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-268)

### Health

In December 2024, Pelosi was hospitalized after fracturing her hip while falling down stairs in high heels during an official trip to [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg").[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-269)[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-270)[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-271) She was there as part of a bipartisan [congressional delegation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_delegation "Congressional delegation") to observe the 80th anniversary of the [Battle of the Bulge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Bulge "Battle of the Bulge").[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-272) On December 14, she underwent [hip replacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_replacement "Hip replacement") surgery at [Landstuhl Regional Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landstuhl_Regional_Medical_Center "Landstuhl Regional Medical Center"), a U.S. military hospital in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany").[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Pelosi#cite_note-273)
